45.0.0.en: 1 Moses was beloved of God and men, blessed in memory, 2 and He gave him glory like the glory of the saints, and made him great, fearful to enemies. By his words he made the signs cease. 3 And He glorified him before kings. He commanded him concerning His people, and showed him His glory. 4 He sanctified him by his faith and his meekness, and chose him from among all men. 5 He made him hear His voice, and brought him into the cloud. 6 He gave him the commandments face to face, the law of life and knowledge, to teach Jacob the covenant, and Israel His judgments.

45.1.0.en: Moses was honored among the saints, opening the door of hope to all believers, for he stumbled on some occasions (Ex 4:13-15; 5:11-23; Num 20:11-12), but he repented and followed God. Therefore God honored him [3] and sanctified him [4].

45.1.1.en: The Lord raised up from his seed a man of mercy, who found grace in the eyes of all flesh, beloved of God and man, Moses, whose memory is blessed [1].

45.1.2.en: The Lord raised up Moses from the seed of Jacob, and here calls him a "man of mercy." He was the first leader of the people of God, whom He chose to free them from the slavery of Pharaoh; with boldness he stood before the wrath of God declaring his love for them, when he said: "Yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written" (Ex 32:32). He interceded for them, giving them priority over himself, as a man of mercy who found grace in the eyes of God and in the eyes of men, not only in his own time but through the generations. God loved him and men loved him; the mere mention of him came to be counted a blessing [1].

45.1.3.en: He made his glory like the glory of the saints, and made him great, so that his enemies fear him [2].

45.1.4.en: He described Moses as equal in glory with the saints. Look to Moses, whose face shone as a reflection of the glory of God upon him (Ex 34:33-35; 2 Cor 3:13), since he spoke with God face to face.

45.1.5.en: The Lord gave him awe before his enemies; it is stated in the Greek manuscript that he was honored like God (who sent him). Moses the prophet, by confronting Pharaoh (Ex 5:1), set a pattern for the prophets after him, who confronted kings with courage and without fear, such as: Samuel with King Saul (1 Sam 15:16), Nathan with King David (2 Sam 12:7-12), Hanani the seer with Asa king of Judah (2 Chr 16:7), Elijah with King Ahab (1 Kgs 17:1), Micaiah the son of Imlah with King Ahab (1 Kgs 22:8), Isaiah with Ahaz, and Jeremiah with Zedekiah.

45.1.6.en: By his words he stopped signs, and the Lord glorified him before kings, and gave him commandments for his people, and showed him His glory [3].

45.1.7.en: He gave him to work signs and wonders (Ps 15-17), and glorified him before kings. "The LORD spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend" (cf. Ex 33:11), delivered to him the law, which is counted an embodiment of the divine wisdom (Ex 20-23), and showed him something of His glory (Ex 24; 33), and entered with him into a covenant.

45.2.0.en: He sanctified him for his faithfulness and meekness, and chose him from among all men [4].

45.2.1.en: He was marked by faithfulness and meekness (Num 12:3), and he owed this to the Holy One who sanctified him with these two traits, and chose him from among all men.

45.3.0.en: He made him hear His voice, and led him in the dark cloud, and gave him the commandments face to face, the law of life and knowledge, to teach Jacob the covenant and Israel His judgments [5].

45.3.1.en: The cloud in which God led him points to his entering into the cloud to hear the words of the Lord on Mount Sinai (Ex 19:16-19; 20:21), and He gave him understanding and a holy life (Deut 4:6; 30:15), so that he might be able to teach Israel (Deut 4:14; Ps 147:19).

45.3.2.en: v Moses also arose and did good with God, and set up a front of faith according to his ability.

45.3.3.en: He increased in lofty beauty through humility, and drew near to God by faith.

45.3.4.en: He became beautiful and enlightened until he became a chosen vessel, for prophecy to use abundantly.

45.3.5.en: He became inward by the love of his soul for God, until He made him like a steward over all His treasury.

45.3.6.en: He loved the people of the Lord in the time of distress and persecution, so he took their reproach and left the wealth of all Egypt[1].

45.4.0.en: 7 He exalted Aaron the holy one, the like of him, his brother of the tribe of Levi. 8 He made for him an everlasting covenant, and gave him the priesthood of the people. He made him happy in splendor, 9 and girded him with a robe of glory. He clothed him with perfection of pride, and strengthened him with instruments of might: 10 the breeches, the long robe and the ephod, and He set about him pomegranates of gold, with many bells round about him, 11 that their sound might ring at his step, that the tinkling might be heard in the temple, as a memorial for the sons of his people. 12 And He gave him the holy garment of gold and blue and purple, the work of a skillful weaver, the breastplate of judgment, in which are the light and the truth. 13 Its weaving was of twisted scarlet, the work of a skillful workman, and upon it precious stones like the engraving of a signet, set in gold, the work of a jewel engraver, engraved upon it the names of the tribes of Israel as a memorial. 14 And on the turban was a crown of gold, engraved upon it the inscription of holiness. It was an ornament of honor, a work of skill, which the eyes love for its beauty. 15 All these were exceedingly beautiful, and there was nothing like them in the age. 16 No one wore them but one of his kindred, his sons and his descendants in every generation. 17 His sacrifices are burned with fire every day, twice without ceasing. 18 Moses consecrated his hands, and anointed him with the holy oil, 19 and it became an everlasting covenant, for him and for his seed as long as heaven lasts, to minister to the Lord, and to practice the priesthood, and to bless his people in His name. 20 He chose him from among all the living, to offer the offering to the Lord, the incense and the sweet savor, as a memorial and an atonement for his people. 21 He established him over His commandments, and gave him authority over the covenants of judgments, to teach Jacob the testimonies, and to enlighten Israel with His law. 22 Strangers gathered against him and envied him in the wilderness, the men of Dathan and Abiram and the congregation of Korah with sharpness and anger. 23 The Lord saw and was not pleased, and destroyed them with the sharpness of His anger. 24 He wrought wonders upon them, and consumed them with the fire of His flame. 25 And He increased Aaron in glory, and gave him an inheritance. He made for them the firstfruits of the earth, 26 and prepared for them before others their fill of bread. They eat of the sacrifices of the Lord, which He gave to him and to his seed. 27 Yet he did not inherit in the land of the people, and had no portion among them, for He Himself is his portion and his inheritance.

45.4.1.en: The Book here covers the personality and role of Aaron more than that of Moses, not because he is greater than Moses, but to affirm that God works in the leaders through the generations, especially the priests. It begins here with Aaron as the first high priest, and ends the discourse with Simon son of Onas the high priest, a contemporary of Ben Sira (Sir 50:1-12).

45.4.2.en: The discourse concerning Aaron as the first of the high priests came in seventeen statements, more than any hero mentioned in this book except the high priest Simon son of Onias (Sir 50:1-21), because this book is considered the only one among the wisdom books that was concerned with the priestly work and liturgical worship.

45.4.3.en: The poem concerning Aaron came in two parts: his garments (Sir 45:6-13), and the sacrifices that he offers (Sir 45:14-22). The garments of splendor and his glorious robe with the rest of the garments point to the Lord Christ, who wraps Himself with His holy Church, which is without blame, as a garment of His that reflects His splendor upon her and sanctifies her. As for the sacrifices, they point to the unique sacrifice of Christ.

45.4.4.en: Moses received the Law, which is based on the existence of a covenant between God and the people, so there came to be a need for holiness, which is a gift of the Holy One, enjoyed by the believers through spiritual worship and the priesthood, which is a shadow of the priesthood of Christ. What Sirach wanted from the series of the heroes of Israel is: the emphasis on faithfulness to God in true worship, and unfaithfulness brings death.

45.4.5.en: He exalted Aaron, a saint like Moses his brother, of the tribe of Levi [6].

45.4.6.en: Aaron was sanctified like his brother. The role of Moses as a prophet was to receive the revelation from God and convey it to the people, while the role of Aaron as a priest was to lift up the repentance of the people and their petitions and sacrifices to God, and in this their work is completed.

45.4.7.en: He made an everlasting covenant with him, and made him priest of the people. He blessed him with a splendid priestly order, and clothed him with a glorious robe[2] [7].

45.4.8.en: Ben Sira stressed that God deposited the gift of the priesthood and the practice of worship with Aaron and his sons. What Ben Sira affirms is that God is the one who appointed the worship of Israel to Himself, presenting His divine blessings to his people; therefore when Dathan, Abiram and Korah usurped the authority of the priests, He punished them (Num 16; 26), for his making atonement for the iniquity of Israel.

45.4.9.en: He clothed him with perfection of pride[3], and established him with symbols of strength, and clothed him with linen breeches and a long robe and an ephod [8].

45.5.0.en: And He set around him pomegranates with many bells of gold around him, which rang with every step he took, and the sound of them was heard as he walked in the temple, as a memorial for the sons of his people [9].

45.6.0.en: And a holy garment of gold and lilies and embroidered purple, and the breastplate of judgment with the Urim and the Thummim, and its weaving was of scarlet, the work of a skillful weaver [10].

45.7.0.en: And upon it precious stones like the engraving of a seal, set in gold, the work of a jewel engraver, engraved according to the number of the tribes of Israel [11].

45.7.1.en: The description of these costly splendid garments occurs in (Ex 28), and God gave wisdom to the craftsmen so that they might make them skillfully, as the names of the tribes of Israel were engraved on precious stones, that is, upon his right shoulder and his left, since all the children of Israel come forward to God through Aaron. And the pomegranates served as bells to alert the children of Israel when he moved, as He also adorned him with the Urim and the Thummim, which are precious stones meaning perfections and lights, and the children of Israel used to inquire of God's mind through the direction of their rays (Ex 28:6).

45.8.0.en: And upon the priestly turban was a crown of gold, in the form of the holy seal, a sign of distinction of honor, made by an expert, a delight of the eyes for the richness of its adornment [12].

45.9.0.en: There was nothing like all this before him in beauty, and no stranger had worn them before; rather his sons and his seed alone wear it continually [13].

45.10.0.en: His sacrifices were whole burnt offerings, perfect, offered every day twice without ceasing [14].

45.10.1.en: The morning sacrifice and the evening sacrifice, which are a burnt offering to the Lord offered on behalf of the people twice daily.

45.11.0.en: Moses is the one who ordained him, and anointed him with the holy oil, and that became an everlasting covenant for him and for his seed forever, to minister to the Lord, to minister as a priest and bless his people in the name of (the Lord) [15].

45.11.1.en: St. Clement of Alexandria[4] compares Aaron the high priest with the sinful woman: 1. Aaron enjoyed his anointing with the holy oil, and that became an everlasting covenant for him and for his descendants (Sir 45:15); and the most precious thing the sinful woman had was the ointment that she poured upon the Lord Christ. 2. Aaron wore a crown of gold (Sir 45:12), and the sinful woman wiped the feet of the Lord with the hair of her head, which is considered the crown and garland of a woman. 3. Since she had not yet entered into communion with the Lord of glory, as a sinner she poured out the tears of repentance.

45.12.0.en: He chose him from among all the living, to offer the offering to the Lord, the incense and the sweet savor as a memorial, and to make atonement for your people [16].

45.13.0.en: The priests were responsible for offering incense and teaching the people and interpreting the law (Deut 31:9-13; 33:10), and they had the authority and the right to consider difficult cases [17] (cf. Deut 17:8-12; 21:5).

45.13.1.en: And He gave him authority by His commandments over the judgments of the law, to teach Jacob the testimonies, and to enlighten Israel concerning His law [17].

45.13.2.en: Sirach makes clear the integration between worship and obedience to the divine commandment, as it is the source of heavenly wisdom.

45.14.0.en: Strangers conspired against him, and envied him in the wilderness, the men who gathered with Dathan and Abiram and the congregation of Korah in wrath and anger [18].

45.14.1.en: Aaron exercised the priesthood for forty years, and the Lord confirmed his priesthood against those who rose up against him, namely Korah, Dathan and Abiram, who tried to offer strange fire to the Lord, so they perished with two hundred and fifty of their company (Num 16), and the Lord's confirmation of his priesthood came by way of the almond rod that blossomed and brought forth buds (Num 17:8).

45.15.0.en: The Lord saw that and was not pleased, so they were destroyed in the wrath of His anger; He wrought wonders against them and consumed them in His blazing fire [19].

45.15.1.en: Ben Sira referred to the rebellion of Korah, Dathan and Abiram who challenged Aaron and Moses (Num 16:3). This company became a wonder, as the earth swallowed them suddenly with the appearance of a fire that destroyed those who ran after them.

45.16.0.en: And He increased Aaron in glory, and gave him an inheritance, and apportioned to him the first of the firstfruits, and prepared for him bread from the firstfruits in abundance [20].

45.16.1.en: The Lord increased Aaron's glory by assigning the Levites to help the priests, and gave the priests a share in the sacrifices (Lev 24:5-9; Num 18:5-9). And since the Lord Himself became their portion and inheritance, the Levites did not inherit a portion in the land of promise (Num 18:20).

45.17.0.en: For they eat of the sacrifices of the Lord, which He gave to him and to his seed [21].

45.18.0.en: Yet he did not inherit in the land of the people, and had no portion among the people, for the Lord Himself is his portion and his inheritance [22]

45.18.1.en: Many ministers lived on a bare sufficiency, yet did not feel want, nor looked for a temporal reward, but enjoyed the divine promise that the Lord Himself is their portion; this is their everlasting inheritance.

45.19.0.en: 28 And Phinehas the son of Eleazar is third in glory, for his zeal in the fear of the Lord, 29 and because he stood up, at the apostasy of the people, with the goodness of the readiness of his soul, and made atonement for Israel. 30 Therefore the Lord gave him the covenant of His peace, that he should be the leader of his people in the holy things, and that to him and to his seed should remain the greatness of the priesthood forever. 31 And He made a covenant with David the son of Jesse of the tribe of Judah, of the inheritance of the kingdom from son to son in his seed, like the inheritance of Aaron and his seed. That He may give you wisdom in your hearts, to judge His people with righteousness, so that their good things may not vanish, nor their glory, throughout their generations.

45.19.1.en: Phinehas is a Hebrew name, whose meaning is "mouth of brass," and he is the son of Eleazar the son of Aaron.

45.19.2.en: After that Phinehas the son of Eleazar is third in glory, when he showed his zeal in the fear of the Lord, and because he stood firm at the apostasy of the people, with the goodness of the zeal of his soul[5], so he made atonement for Israel [23].

45.19.3.en: By his saying "third in glory" he means the third generation from Aaron (Ex 6:25), and he is as the heir in the priesthood in the Old Testament. The source of his honor is his commitment to the worship of God and setting boundaries between the believers and the worshipers of idols (Num 25:1-9). He was jealous with the jealousy of the Lord when the people committed adultery with the daughters of Moab, so he killed Zimri the son of Salu, chief of a house of the Simeonites, with the Midianite woman Cozbi the daughter of Zur, and the plague was stayed, and he received from the Lord a covenant of peace for him and for his sons, and their headship of the priesthood continued until the destruction of the temple in AD 70 [24].

45.19.4.en: Therefore (the Lord) established with him a covenant of peace, that he might be in charge of the sanctuary[6] and a leader of his people, so that to him and to his seed would remain the greatness of the priesthood throughout the ages [24].

45.19.5.en: And a covenant was made with David the son of Jesse of the tribe of Judah, but the inheritance of the kingdom passes from son to son only, whereas the inheritance of Aaron is for his seed [25].

45.19.6.en: When Sirach spoke of Aaron the high priest and Phinehas the priest, he wanted to affirm the distinction between the Aaronic priestly covenant and the Davidic royal covenant, to affirm that the priesthood belongs to one tribe, which is the tribe of Levi, and kingship belongs to the tribe of Judah. The two covenants are complementary, but it is not the right of the priest to sit as king upon the throne of Israel, nor the right of the king to usurp the priestly work. 1. If the tribe of David alone had the kingship, yet its inheritance is handed over from one son to one son, whereas the inheritance of Aaron is not for a son but for his seed [25]. 2. The kingship of Israel and its priesthood appeared in the visions of Zechariah the prophet not as one olive tree but two olive trees (Zech 4:3), so that one tribe would not usurp what belongs to the other. And their integration was fulfilled as a symbol of the Lord Christ, who alone is King of kings (Rev 19:16) and at the same time the heavenly High Priest (Heb 8:1).

45.19.7.en: The priestly and the royal work shine with light through the oil of God's grace that the people of God may enjoy enlightenment, while the Lord Christ is the light of the world (Jn 9:5) who grants the believers from all peoples to become the light of the world (Mt 5:14). 3. Under the Law the people of God needed the two olive trees together, one at the right of the bowl full of the oil of grace, and the other at its left (Zech 4:3). This integration of working together appeared before the Law in the person of Melchizedek, who is king of Salem and at the same time priest of the Most High God (Heb 7:1).

45.19.8.en: May the Lord give you wisdom in your hearts, that you may judge His people with righteousness, so that their good things may not vanish, and their glory remain throughout their generations [26].

45.19.9.en: If the seed of Aaron enjoyed the divine covenant for the practice of the priestly work, yet they needed prayer to be made for them; Sirach felt this, so he prayed for them, saying: "May the Lord give you wisdom in your hearts to judge His people with righteousness" [26].

45.19.10.en: This is what the deacon asks of the people in the Divine Liturgy and the liturgies, saying: "Pray and ask for our father the Pope the Patriarch," as he asks the same concerning the bishops, priests and deacons.

45.19.11.en: Why did Ben Sira pray for the high priests and the priests who were of the seed of Aaron? Without doubt Sirach's soul was bitter, because some persons bought the priesthood from the Seleucid kings in the second century BC to serve in the temple in Jerusalem. If the priest prays, asking blessing for the people, Ben Sira touches the blessing that descends upon the priests of God for the sake of their service to the people of God.

45.19.12.en: v Phinehas arose and made a triumph on account of the fornicators and showed his zeal: and how near he was to God.

45.19.13.en: His work bears witness to how vigilant his conscience was, for he drove fornication out of the camp by his righteousness.

45.19.14.en: Look at his deed, and from it learn his love: how much he cared to remove evil from his people.

45.19.15.en: His soul was holy and pure and hated fornication, so he threw the spear at the fornicators to put an end to evil.

45.19.16.en: He stood in prayer and held back death from many, and by the two persons whom he killed he saved thousands lest they be destroyed[7].

45.19.17.en: St. Jacob of Serugh Inspired by Sirach 45

45.20.s.en: Reveal to me Your plan for me!

45.20.0.en: v How wonderful, how Pharaoh with all his might feared the Hebrew child Moses!

45.20.1.en: He was brought up in the house of the violent Pharaoh, and did not realize that the child who was in his house was a man of mercy!

45.20.2.en: Mercy did not leave his heart from his childhood to the day of his repose!

45.20.3.en: You granted him the spirit of strength and holiness, and he worked signs before kings.

45.20.4.en: You showed him Your glory and delivered to him the law.

45.20.5.en: You inclined Your ear, and found sweet his intercession for the people before You.

45.20.6.en: He was the object of Your delight for his faithfulness and meekness.

45.20.7.en: v You made a covenant with Aaron, and he put on the splendid garment of the priesthood.

45.20.8.en: With every step in the temple the heavenly ones rejoice at the sound of the bells on the hem of his garment!

45.20.9.en: He carries on his breastplate the names of the twelve tribes.

45.20.10.en: There was engraved on his turban "Holy to the LORD."

45.20.11.en: You accepted his daily sacrifices of the day and the night and his fragrant incense.

45.20.12.en: You raised him in the eyes of the heavenly and the earthly, since You did not give him a portion in the land of promise, for You are his portion.

45.20.13.en: v The heart of Phinehas, the grandson of Aaron, was kindled with the fear of God.

45.20.14.en: He would not accept silence over a priest who committed fornication with a pagan woman.

45.20.15.en: The soul of Phinehas was sanctified, and by his pure prayer death was held back from many!

45.20.16.en: What do I ask except that You lead my life in holiness and faithfulness.

45.20.17.en: So that I may have a portion in Your eternal embrace!
